title: The AI Champion Playbook: Knowledge Transfer That Actually Sticks (2026)

questions.question: What primary artifact does recommend_artifact choose for an L2 practitioner with procedural knowledge?
options: A session, because practitioners should learn only synchronously
A decision aid, because code is too detailed for L2
A reference implementation, followed by an eval harness
An eval harness alone, because procedure and evaluation are identical
questions.explanation: The routing table maps (L2_PRACTITIONER, PROCEDURAL) to REFERENCE_IMPL with EVAL_HARNESS as the next artifact. A runnable pattern grounds the procedure and the harness checks it.

questions.question: What recommendation does recommend_artifact return for an L1 aware audience needing procedural knowledge?
options: An eval harness followed by a skill file
A reference implementation with no synchronous teaching
A decision aid only, because L1 users cannot attend sessions
A session followed by a decision aid, so the demo produces a reusable takeaway
questions.explanation: L1 procedural knowledge is routed to SESSION, with DECISION_AID as the next artifact. The live demonstration meets the audience where it is, while the decision aid preserves the learning.

questions.question: Where does evaluate_pilot block RAG Q&A over internal policy docs?
options: Gate 2 Quality, because it has no eval harness even though Gate 1 passed
Gate 1 Feasibility, because the prototype has no documented failure cases
Gate 3 Transfer, because the colleague has not reproduced it
No gate; the pilot may scale from a working prototype
questions.explanation: The RAG pilot has a working prototype and documented failures, so Gate 1 passes. It has no eval harness, making Gate 2 the first blocked gate and the required next artifact.

questions.question: Why is the automated meeting-note summarizer blocked at Gate 2?
options: Gate 1 fails because its prototype is missing
The harness exists, but its 61% pass rate is below the 80% quality threshold
Gate 3 passes automatically when the eval harness exists
The quality threshold is ignored when a decision aid is already present
questions.explanation: The pilot has a prototype, documented failures, and an eval harness, so feasibility passes. Its 61% result is below the configured 80% threshold, so evaluate_pilot blocks at G2_QUALITY.

questions.question: What verdict does evaluate_pilot return for the Code review assistant with an 87% pass rate and colleague reproduction?
options: Blocked at Gate 2 because every quality score below 90% fails
Blocked at Gate 3 because a reference implementation is not required for builders
All three gates passed; the pilot is ready to scale
Blocked at Gate 1 because the model name is provider-specific
questions.explanation: The prototype and failure cases pass G1, 87% exceeds the 80% threshold for G2, and the decision aid, reference implementation, and colleague reproduction pass G3.

questions.question: What does evaluate_pilot require first for Ticket-triage agent, which has neither a prototype nor documented failures?
options: An eval harness and 80% pass rate before any prototype is built
A decision aid, because transfer must precede feasibility
A colleague reproduction run from an empty implementation
A working prototype and documented failure cases for Gate 1 feasibility
questions.explanation: Gate 1 requires both has_working_prototype and failure_cases_documented. evaluate_pilot stops there and lists those two artifacts before quality or transfer can be assessed.
